_note: How the outside world answers what the business does: social posts, marketing email, replies to customers, new and ended products, and the optional quality score. Read by sim/audience.mjs and sim/core.mjs. Every number has a value, a one-line why, and a source: a link, or "assumption" when we have no source. Change a value and re-run; docs/consequences.md explains each one in plain words.

base_reach.why: Share of followers who see an ordinary company post over its life. Organic reach is commonly quoted at a few to ten per cent.

decay_days.why: Hot-score feed: views fall away exponentially with this time constant (photo posts live longer than short posts).
decay_days.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.11581 (OASIS hot-score feed; the constants are ours)

window_days.why: After a week a post is effectively off every feed.

picture_on_mutter.why: A short post with a picture is seen more than one without (squint always has a picture).

hour_factor.why: Night is 00-06, morning 07-09, day 10-16, evening 17-21, late 22-23: people scroll before work and after dinner.

weekday_factor.why: Sunday first. Weekends have a little more scrolling time.

length.why: Very short posts say nothing; very long ones are skipped.

names_product.why: A post about a real thing is shared more than a general one; it also sends its visitors to that product.

fits_event.why: A post about something happening now (an active world event) travels further.

offer.why: A discount or code gets more likes, more clicks and more of those clicks buy.

fatigue.why: Posting more than three times a week lowers every post's reach (followers mute or scroll past); each extra post the same day reaches 60% of the one before.

virality_sd.why: Spread of luck between posts (log-normal): some posts simply do better.

comments_per_like.why: Comments are much rarer than likes.

repost_rate.why: Reposts per person reached; short-post networks repost more.

reach_per_repost.why: Extra people each repost reaches (one generation only).

visit_rate.why: Visits to the shop per person reached (link taps).

follow_rate.why: New followers per person reached who did not follow yet.

drift_per_day.why: With no company post on a network for 14 days, followers drift away at this share a day.

max_comment_records.why: At most this many comment records are written per post (the count can be higher); keeps the feed readable.

conversion.why: Share of visits that become an order. Shopify global figures run from about 1.4% (home) to 4.9% (beauty).

average_order_value.why: Used only to estimate the revenue shown on a post or email when no product is named; the real revenue is in the impact.

min_customer_recipients.why: A sent email to three or more customers counts as marketing mail; fewer is a personal email.

open_rate.why: Share of recipients who open a marketing email.

click_rate.why: Share of openers who click through to the shop.

unsubscribe_rate.why: Share of recipients who unsubscribe after an ordinary mail.

not_opted_in_unsubscribe.why: Mailing someone who never opted in makes them far likelier to unsubscribe.

fatigue.why: More than two marketing mails a fortnight: fewer opens, more unsubscribes.

decay_days.why: Most opens happen in the first day or two.

window_days.why: After four days a marketing mail is buried.

fast_hours.why: A public reply or private message within four hours counts as fast.

slow_hours.why: After two days a reply still helps a little.

min_helpful_chars.why: Shorter than this is not a helpful answer.

points_fast.why: Customer memory points for a fast, helpful reply (the same scale as sim.json customers).

points_slow.why: Memory points for a helpful reply that came late.

points_unhelpful.why: A curt reply does slight harm.

public_complaint_reputation.why: A fast, helpful public answer to a complaint lifts reputation (0 to 1 scale) a little; other people see it.

email_csat.why: Satisfaction (1 to 5) for a person's email reply to a customer, by speed and whether it addressed their order or topic.

novelty_boost.why: A newly launched product sells up to 2.5 times its settled rate, fading away.

novelty_days.why: Time constant of the novelty fade.

cannibalisation.why: Share of a new product's sales taken from the rest of the range rather than new.

switch_share.why: Share of an ended product's demand that moves to products in the same category; the rest is lost.

price_elasticity_in_category.why: A new product priced above its category's typical price sells less, in proportion.

range.why: An optional judged quality score (0 to 1) maps onto this range of response; 0.5 or no score gives 1.
